digest.component_or_area: codebase-wide consolidation epic (store paths, lifecycle cascade, commands, reconciler, llm, mcp)
propositions: Duplicated business logic exists in 2-7 places across the codebase; fixes land in one copy while twins remain broken, causing multi-ticket arrival patterns
Consolidation must collapse each duplicated computation into exactly one shared module implementation, verified by construct-uniqueness guards that assert on distinctive atoms not internals
Consolidation children must preserve all pinned observable behaviour (pinning tests pass unchanged) and achieve net-negative non-test lines across all children

Eight merged consolidation children show net +241 non-test lines (add=818, del=577) with only three achieving negative deltas, suggesting acceptance criterion AC3 is measuring a proxy that correct consolidation work legitimately violates

Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 were written pre-implementation and empirically fail for correct work (AC2 fails for 9/23 children due to duplicated test blocks being removed; AC3 measured +2449 across full set) and should be restated to measure actual guarantees (one implementation per construct, no silent behaviour divergence) rather than proxy metrics
